Issue Number: close #53837

Problem Summary:

### What changed and how does it work?

Optimize memory allocations to save CPU time in the hot path.

Master:
```
go test -run=^$ -bench=Record -benchmem -benchtime=30s
goos: linux
goarch: amd64
pkg: github.com/pingcap/tidb/pkg/table/tables
cpu: AMD Ryzen 5 3600 6-Core Processor
BenchmarkAddRecordInPipelinedDML-12       	    1050	  28595471 ns/op	      2860 ns/record	 7818797 B/op	  161352 allocs/op
BenchmarkRemoveRecordInPipelinedDML-12    	    2382	  12638043 ns/op	      1264 ns/record	 2848806 B/op	   90455 allocs/op
BenchmarkUpdateRecordInPipelinedDML-12    	    1844	  16815817 ns/op	      1682 ns/record	 8296254 B/op	  110608 allocs/op
PASS
ok  	github.com/pingcap/tidb/pkg/table/tables	261.149s
```

```

PASS

```

issue_context.title: Optimize slice allocations in the hot path
issue_context.body:
## Enhancement
Some slice allocations can be costly. We can reuse old slices to save CPU time.

review_comments:
But there is no need for `GetRowToCheckCloned()`. All these slices are temporary variables. Even if a slice is obtained from `GetRowToCheck`, it still can be mistakenly accessed outside its expected lifetime. 

The best option I could think of is to use a clear name that everyone would understand this is a temporary slice. So I chose the pattern `buffer.xxx` everywhere.

> use a clear name that everyone would understand

Using clearer naming is also feasible. If there are no better hard constraint methods, I believe we need to add comments and warnings in all places where these buffered slices are used, to avoid additionally referencing the input slice and to highlight the related lifetime risks. 

This is actually the most difficult part (or the limitation of Golang). The way mentioned above using functions is essentially an attempt to achieve this goal as much as possible.
Does the opt cost visible cpu time? I think it'll be a tradeoff between extensionbility and performance.
Yes. IIRC allocating the opt takes some time.
